items.title: Frank Wess interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995
items.q: So eventually he got Sonny and Joe Williams came in at the same time you know. So that’s when, the band really started to get together you know.

ctx.x: Well there were only two, Gus Johnson and Gus Johnson got sick so we were trying out different drummers, and they didn’t make it. He even called Papa Jo back, but Papa Jo didn’t fit with that band you know, it was a different thing. So one day he says, “hey Magic, come over, I got a little drummer down here, let’s go catch him.” So we went down to the Regal Theater in Chicago, me and Bas’, and Sonny Payne was there with I think maybe Erskine Hawkins or somebody. And he say, “What you think, man?” I say, “Yeah, he…

items.title: Frank Wess interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995
items.q: I had forgotten actually, how good the band was... I got Eddie Jones in the band, Bill Hughes, Sonny Cohn, Eric Dixon, Thad Jones... I can’t think, oh Al Aarons. Yeah I got a whole lot of people in the band, you know.

ctx.x: What was it like playing in different parts of the world with the Basie band?

Oh, we always had a good following. And the band was hot. We were in one of the best bands Basie ever had. And that’s the band that made him rich, you know. The band was tight. I had forgotten actually, how good the band was until I was listening to those Mosaic recordings. And then it came back to me, how good that band was. It was like one person playing, you know. Everybody was—it was a good band. Well Basie, he knew how to do that. You know he didn’t fault nobody. He just let it stay there until the cats got…
Were you happy switching from the tenor to the alto?
